sanskrit: pramatto dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putro duryodhanas tadā nābhyabhāṣat subalajaṃ bhāṣamāṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son Duryodhana, his mind distracted, did not then address Śakuni, the son of Subala, though he spoke to him again and again.

sanskrit: anekāgraṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā śakuniḥ pratyabhāṣata duryodhana kutomūlaṃ niḥśvasann iva gacchasi
english: Seeing him thus scattered in mind, Śakuni spoke to him: "Duryodhana, what is the root of this — why do you walk sighing like one in grief?"

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca dṛṣṭvemāṃ pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ yudhiṣṭhiravaśānugām jitām astrapratāpena śvetāśvasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Duryodhana said: Having seen this entire earth brought under Yudhiṣṭhira's sway — won by the martial prowess of the great-souled Arjuna, the white-horsed hero —

sanskrit: taṃ ca yajñaṃ tathābhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthasya mātula yathā śakrasya deveṣu tathābhūtaṃ mahādyute
english: and having witnessed that sacrifice of Pārtha conducted in such a manner — brilliant uncle, it was like Indra's sacrifice among the gods —

sanskrit: amarṣeṇa susaṃpūrṇo dahyamāno divāniśam śuciśukrāgame kāle śuṣye toyam ivālpakam
english: I am filled entirely with indignation, burning day and night — as a shallow pool dries up when the hot season of Śukra arrives.

sanskrit: paśya sātvatamukhyena śiśupālaṃ nipātitam na ca tatra pumān āsīt kaś cit tasya padānugaḥ
english: See how Śiśupāla was struck down by the foremost of the Sātvatas — and not a single man there stood to follow him in support.

sanskrit: dahyamānā hi rājānaḥ pāṇḍavotthena vahninā kṣāntavanto 'parādhaṃ taṃ ko hi taṃ kṣantum arhati
english: The kings, burning in the fire kindled by the Pāṇḍavas, forgave that offense. But who truly deserves to forgive such a thing?

sanskrit: vāsudevena tat karma tathāyuktaṃ mahat kṛtam siddhaṃ ca pāṇḍaveyānāṃ pratāpena mahātmanām
english: That great deed was carried out so fittingly by Vāsudeva, and succeeded through the glory of the great-souled sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tathā hi ratnāny ādāya vividhāni nṛpā nṛpam upatiṣṭhanti kaunteyaṃ vaiśyā iva karapradāḥ
english: And so kings bearing various treasures attend upon the son of Kuntī, paying tribute like merchants paying taxes to a king.

sanskrit: śriyaṃ tathāvidhāṃ dṛṣṭvā jvalantīm iva pāṇḍave amarṣavaśam āpanno dahye 'ham atathocitaḥ
english: Having seen such blazing prosperity in the Pāṇḍava, I am seized by indignation and burn — I who am not suited to bear this.

sanskrit: vahnim eva pravekṣyāmi bhakṣayiṣyāmi vā viṣam apo vāpi pravekṣyāmi na hi śakṣyāmi jīvitum
english: I shall enter fire, or consume poison, or plunge into water — I cannot go on living.

sanskrit: ko hi nāma pumāṃl loke marṣayiṣyati sattvavān sapatnān ṛdhyato dṛṣṭvā hānim ātmana eva ca
english: What man of spirit in this world would tolerate it — watching his rivals prosper while he himself declines?

sanskrit: so 'haṃ na strī na cāpy astrī na pumān nāpumān api yo 'haṃ tāṃ marṣayāmy adya tādṛśīṃ śriyam āgatām
english: I am neither woman nor neuter, neither man nor eunuch — yet today I endure such prosperity come to others. What then am I?

sanskrit: īśvaratvaṃ pṛthivyāś ca vasumattāṃ ca tādṛśīm yajñaṃ ca tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā mādṛśaḥ ko na saṃjvaret
english: Having witnessed such sovereignty over the earth, such wealth, and such a sacrifice as that — who like me would not be consumed by envy?

sanskrit: aśaktaś caika evāhaṃ tām āhartuṃ nṛpaśriyam sahāyāṃś ca na paśyāmi tena mṛtyuṃ vicintaye
english: Alone and unable to seize that royal splendor, seeing no allies, I contemplate death.

sanskrit: daivam eva paraṃ manye pauruṣaṃ tu nirarthakam dṛṣṭvā kuntīsute śubhrāṃ śriyaṃ tām āhṛtāṃ tathā
english: I think fate alone is paramount; human effort is meaningless — having seen that resplendent prosperity thus acquired by the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: kṛto yatno mayā pūrvaṃ vināśe tasya saubala tac ca sarvam atikramya sa vṛddho 'psv iva paṅkajam
english: I made effort before for his destruction, O Saubala — yet he has surpassed all of that and grown, like a lotus in water.

sanskrit: tena daivaṃ paraṃ manye pauruṣaṃ tu nirarthakam dhārtarāṣṭrā hi hīyante pārthā vardhanti nityaśaḥ
english: Therefore I consider fate supreme and human effort pointless — the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra diminish while the sons of Pṛthā ever grow.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ śriyaṃ ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sabhāṃ tāṃ ca tathāvidhām rakṣibhiś cāvahāsaṃ taṃ paritapye yathāgninā
english: I, who have seen that prosperity and that assembly so magnificent, and the mockery by the guards — I am scorched as if by fire.

sanskrit: sa mām abhyanujānīhi mātulādya suduḥkhitam amarṣaṃ ca samāviṣṭaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭre nivedaya
english: Therefore, uncle, give me leave — today I am deeply sorrowful and filled with indignation. Convey this to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca duryodhana na te 'marṣaḥ kāryaḥ prati yudhiṣṭhiram bhāgadheyāni hi svāni pāṇḍavā bhuñjate sadā
english: Śakuni said: Duryodhana, you should not harbor indignation toward Yudhiṣṭhira — the Pāṇḍavas merely enjoy what is rightfully their own portion.

sanskrit: anekair abhyupāyaiś ca tvayārabdhāḥ purāsakṛt vimuktāś ca naravyāghrā bhāgadheyapuraskṛtāḥ
english: Those tiger-like men were attacked by you before through many schemes, yet they escaped — their portion of fate safeguarding them.

sanskrit: tair labdhā draupadī bhāryā drupadaś ca sutaiḥ saha sahāyaḥ pṛthivīlābhe vāsudevaś ca vīryavān
english: By them was won Draupadī as wife, and Drupada together with his sons as allies in gaining the earth, and the mighty Vāsudeva too.

sanskrit: labdhaś ca nābhibhūto 'rthaḥ pitryo 'ṃśaḥ pṛthivīpate vivṛddhas tejasā teṣāṃ tatra kā paridevanā
english: And their paternal share of wealth, once obtained, has not been overpowered — it has grown through their own glory, O lord of earth. What cause for lament is there?

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayena gāṇḍīvam akṣayyau ca maheṣudhī labdhāny astrāṇi divyāni tarpayitvā hutāśanam
english: By Dhanañjaya was the Gāṇḍīva bow obtained, and the two inexhaustible quivers, and divine weapons — after propitiating the fire-god.

sanskrit: tena kārmukamukhyena bāhuvīryeṇa cātmanaḥ kṛtā vaśe mahīpālās tatra kā paridevanā
english: With that foremost of bows and by the strength of his own arms, kings of the earth were brought under his sway. What cause for lament is there?

sanskrit: agnidāhān mayaṃ cāpi mokṣayitvā sa dānavam sabhāṃ tāṃ kārayām āsa savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ
english: Having rescued Maya the demon from being burned by fire, the ambidextrous Arjuna, scorcher of foes, had him build that assembly hall.

sanskrit: tena caiva mayenoktāḥ kiṃkarā nāma rākṣasāḥ vahanti tāṃ sabhāṃ bhīmās tatra kā paridevanā
english: And by that Maya were summoned the Rākṣasas called Kimkaras — those terrible ones bear that assembly hall. What cause for lament is there?

sanskrit: yac cāsahāyatāṃ rājann uktavān asi bhārata tan mithyā bhrātaro hīme sahāyās te mahārathāḥ
english: As for what you said about having no allies, O king, O Bharata — that is false. These brothers of yours are your allies, great warriors all.

sanskrit: droṇas tava maheṣvāsaḥ saha putreṇa dhīmatā sūtaputraś ca rādheyo gautamaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Droṇa, your great archer, along with his wise son; and the son of a charioteer, Rādheya; and Gautama — all great warriors.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca saha sodaryaiḥ saumadattiś ca vīryavān etais tvaṃ sahitaḥ sarvair jaya kṛtsnāṃ vasuṃdharām
english: And I together with my brothers, and the valiant son of Somadatta — united with all of these, go and conquer the entire earth.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca tvayā ca sahito rājann etaiś cānyair mahārathaiḥ etān eva vijeṣyāmi yadi tvam anumanyase
english: Duryodhana said: Together with you, O king, and with these and other great warriors, I shall conquer them — if you give your approval.

sanskrit: eteṣu vijiteṣv adya bhaviṣyati mahī mama sarve ca pṛthivīpālāḥ sabhā sā ca mahādhanā
english: When these are conquered, the earth will be mine, and all the kings of the earth, and that hall of immense wealth.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca dhanaṃjayo vāsudevo bhīmaseno yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca drupadaś ca sahātmajaiḥ
english: Śakuni said: Dhanañjaya, Vāsudeva, Bhīmasena, Yudhiṣṭhira, Nakula, Sahadeva, and Drupada together with his sons —

sanskrit: naite yudhi balāj jetuṃ śakyāḥ suragaṇair api mahārathā maheṣvāsāḥ kṛtāstrā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: these cannot be conquered by force in battle even by the hosts of gods — great warriors, mighty archers, masters of weapons, mad with the lust for battle.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu tad vijānāmi vijetuṃ yena śakyate yudhiṣṭhiraṃ svayaṃ rājaṃs tan nibodha juṣasva ca
english: But I know the means by which Yudhiṣṭhira himself can be conquered, O king. Hear it and act upon it.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca apramādena suhṛdām anyeṣāṃ ca mahātmanām yadi śakyā vijetuṃ te tan mamācakṣva mātula
english: Duryodhana said: If they can be conquered without harm to friends and other noble ones, then tell me how, uncle.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca dyūtapriyaś ca kaunteyo na ca jānāti devitum samāhūtaś ca rājendro na śakṣyati nivartitum
english: Śakuni said: The son of Kuntī is fond of dice yet does not know how to play; and once challenged, the lord of kings will not be able to refuse.

sanskrit: devane kuśalaś cāhaṃ na me 'sti sadṛśo bhuvi triṣu lokeṣu kaunteyaṃ taṃ tvaṃ dyūte samāhvaya
english: I am skilled at gambling — there is none equal to me on earth or in the three worlds. Challenge that son of Kuntī to a game of dice.

sanskrit: tasyākṣakuśalo rājann ādāsye 'ham asaṃśayam rājyaṃ śriyaṃ ca tāṃ dīptāṃ tvadarthaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: I, skilled with dice, will without doubt win from him his kingdom and that blazing wealth, for your sake, O bull among men.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu sarvaṃ tvaṃ rājñe duryodhana nivedaya anujñātas tu te pitrā vijeṣye taṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: Present all of this to the king, Duryodhana. With your father's permission, I shall conquer him — of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca tvam eva kurumukhyāya dhṛtarāṣṭrāya saubala nivedaya yathānyāyaṃ nāhaṃ śakṣye niśaṃsitum
english: Duryodhana said: You yourself convey this properly to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, foremost of the Kurus, O Saubala — I will not be able to declare it myself.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca anubhūya tu rājñas taṃ rājasūyaṃ mahākratum yudhiṣṭhirasya nṛpater gāndhārīputrasaṃyutaḥ
english: Vaishampyana said: Having witnessed that great Rājasūya sacrifice of king Yudhiṣṭhira, together with the son of Gāndhārī,

sanskrit: priyakṛn matam ājñāya pūrvaṃ duryodhanasya tat prajñācakṣuṣam āsīnaṃ śakuniḥ saubalas tadā
english: Śakuni of Subala's line, knowing before what would please Duryodhana, then approached Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who sat with the eye of wisdom —

sanskrit: duryodhanavacaḥ śrutvā dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janādhipam upagamya mahāprājñaṃ śakunir vākyam abravīt
english: Having heard Duryodhana's words, Śakuni went to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, and spoke to that greatly wise one.

sanskrit: duryodhano mahārāja vivarṇo hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ dīnaś cintāparaś caiva tad viddhi bharatarṣabha
english: "Duryodhana, O great king, is pale, wan, and emaciated, dejected and sunk in worry — know this, O bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: na vai parīkṣase samyag asahyaṃ śatrusaṃbhavam jyeṣṭhaputrasya śokaṃ tvaṃ kimarthaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: "You do not examine properly this unbearable anguish that arises from his enemies. Why do you not perceive the sorrow of your eldest son?"

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca duryodhana kutomūlaṃ bhṛśam ārto 'si putraka śrotavyaś cen mayā so 'rtho brūhi me kurunandana
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Duryodhana, my son, what is the root of your distress — you who are so deeply afflicted? If it is a matter I should hear, tell me, O joy of the Kurus."

sanskrit: ayaṃ tvāṃ śakuniḥ prāha vivarṇaṃ hariṇaṃ kṛśam cintayaṃś ca na paśyāmi śokasya tava saṃbhavam
english: "This Śakuni describes you as pale, wan, and emaciated, brooding — yet I myself cannot perceive the source of your grief."

sanskrit: aiśvaryaṃ hi mahat putra tvayi sarvaṃ samarpitam bhrātaraḥ suhṛdaś caiva nācaranti tavāpriyam
english: "For great sovereignty has been entrusted entirely to you, my son. Your brothers and friends do nothing displeasing to you."

sanskrit: ācchādayasi prāvārān aśnāsi piśitaudanam ājāneyā vahanti tvāṃ kenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: "You wear fine robes, you eat meat and fine food, thoroughbred horses carry you — why then are you wan and thin?"

sanskrit: śayanāni mahārhāṇi yoṣitaś ca manoramāḥ guṇavanti ca veśmāni vihārāś ca yathāsukham
english: "Couches of great worth, charming women, houses full of fine things, and pleasures as you wish —

sanskrit: devānām iva te sarvaṃ vāci baddhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ sa dīna iva durdharṣaḥ kasmāc chocasi putraka
english: all of this is bound to your word as if to that of the gods — no doubt of it. Why then, O unconquerable one, do you grieve like a helpless man, my son?"

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca aśnāmy ācchādaye cāhaṃ yathā kupuruṣas tathā amarṣaṃ dhāraye cograṃ titikṣan kālaparyayam
english: Duryodhana said: "I eat and dress as an inferior man does, and I endure fierce indignation, tolerating the turn of time."

sanskrit: amarṣaṇaḥ svāḥ prakṛtīr abhibhūya pare sthitāḥ kleśān mumukṣuḥ parajān sa vai puruṣa ucyate
english: "He who, unable to endure, sees his own subjects overcome by others and seeks release from those afflictions by conquering the enemy — he truly is called a man."

sanskrit: saṃtoṣo vai śriyaṃ hanti abhimānaś ca bhārata anukrośabhaye cobhe yair vṛto nāśnute mahat
english: "Contentment destroys prosperity, as does arrogance, O Bharata; and both compassion and fear — he who is bound by these does not attain greatness."

sanskrit: na mām avati tad bhuktaṃ śriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhire jvalantīm iva kaunteye vivarṇakaraṇīṃ mama
english: "The food I eat gives me no comfort, having seen that blazing prosperity in Yudhiṣṭhira — in the son of Kuntī — the very sight of which drains my color."

sanskrit: sapatnān ṛdhyato ''tmānaṃ hīyamānaṃ niśāmya ca adṛśyām api kaunteye sthitāṃ paśyann ivodyatām tasmād ahaṃ vivarṇaś ca dīnaś ca hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: "Watching my rivals prosper and myself decline, and seeing — though it be invisible — prosperity standing poised in the son of Kuntī as if raised aloft — therefore I am pale, dejected, wan, and thin."

sanskrit: aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi snātakā gṛhamedhinaḥ triṃśaddāsīka ekaiko yān bibharti yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "Eighty-eight thousand learned householders who have completed their student-vows — each one attended by thirty slave-girls — are maintained by Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: daśānyāni sahasrāṇi nityaṃ tatrānnam uttamam bhuñjate rukmapātrībhir yudhiṣṭhiraniveśane
english: "Another ten thousand daily eat the finest food from golden dishes in Yudhiṣṭhira's household."

sanskrit: kadalīmṛgamokāni kṛṣṇaśyāmāruṇāni ca kāmbojaḥ prāhiṇot tasmai parārdhyān api kambalān
english: "The Kāmbojas sent him priceless woolen blankets — those of banana-colored deer-brown, dark black, and red hues."

sanskrit: rathayoṣidgavāśvasya śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ triṃśataṃ coṣṭravāmīnāṃ śatāni vicaranty uta
english: "By the hundreds and thousands roam chariots, women, cattle, and horses; and thirty hundreds of camel-mares go about as well."

sanskrit: pṛthagvidhāni ratnāni pārthivāḥ pṛthivīpate āharan kratumukhye 'smin kuntīputrāya bhūriśaḥ
english: "Kings brought diverse and abundant jewels of every kind to the son of Kuntī at this foremost of sacrifices, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: na kva cid dhi mayā dṛṣṭas tādṛśo naiva ca śrutaḥ yādṛg dhanāgamo yajñe pāṇḍuputrasya dhīmataḥ
english: "Nowhere have I seen nor heard of such an influx of wealth as at the sacrifice of that wise son of Pāṇḍu."

sanskrit: aparyantaṃ dhanaughaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā śatror ahaṃ nṛpa śarma naivādhigacchāmi cintayāno 'niśaṃ vibho
english: "Having seen that boundless flood of my enemy's wealth, O king, O lord, I find no peace, brooding on it ceaselessly."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā vāṭadhānāś ca gomantaḥ śatasaṃghaśaḥ traikharvaṃ balim ādāya dvāri tiṣṭhanti vāritāḥ
english: "Brahmins and traders bearing cattle, in groups of hundreds, carrying tribute of three hundred million stood at the gate but were turned away."

sanskrit: kamaṇḍalūn upādāya jātarūpamayāñ śubhān evaṃ baliṃ samādāya praveśaṃ lebhire tataḥ
english: "Taking up their water-pots made of pure gold, beautiful ones, and thus taking up their tribute, they then gained entry."

sanskrit: yan naiva madhu śakrāya dhārayanty amarastriyaḥ tad asmai kāṃsyam āhārṣīd vāruṇaṃ kalaśodadhiḥ
english: "Even honey that the celestial women do not ordinarily preserve for Indra — the ocean of Varuṇa's jars brought that in bronze vessels for him."

sanskrit: śaikyaṃ rukmasahasrasya bahuratnavibhūṣitam dṛṣṭvā ca mama tat sarvaṃ jvararūpam ivābhavat
english: "A golden net worth a thousand gold pieces, adorned with many jewels — upon seeing all of that, it all felt to me like the burning of a fever."

sanskrit: gṛhītvā tat tu gacchanti samudrau pūrvadakṣiṇau tathaiva paścimaṃ yānti gṛhītvā bharatarṣabha
english: "Taking their portion, they depart toward the eastern and southern oceans; and likewise taking their portion they go westward, O bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: uttaraṃ tu na gacchanti vinā tāta patatribhiḥ idaṃ cādbhutam atrāsīt tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: "But northward they do not go without winged birds to guide them, dear father. And there was something wondrous here — hear me as I tell it."

sanskrit: pūrṇe śatasahasre tu viprāṇāṃ pariviṣyatām sthāpitā tatra saṃjñābhūc chaṅkho dhmāyati nityaśaḥ
english: "When a full hundred thousand Brahmins had been served, a conch was installed there as a signal and it was blown unceasingly."

sanskrit: muhur muhuḥ praṇadatas tasya śaṅkhasya bhārata uttamaṃ śabdam aśrauṣaṃ tato romāṇi me 'hṛṣan
english: "From that conch sounding again and again, O Bharata, I heard a supreme sound, and then my hairs stood on end."

sanskrit: pārthivair bahubhiḥ kīrṇam upasthānaṃ didṛkṣubhiḥ sarvaratnāny upādāya pārthivā vai janeśvara
english: "The court was thronged with many kings wishing to see it, and those kings, having brought all their jewels, O lord of men —"

sanskrit: yajñe tasya mahārāja pāṇḍuputrasya dhīmataḥ vaiśyā iva mahīpālā dvijātipariveṣakāḥ
english: "at the sacrifice of that wise son of Pāṇḍu, O great king, the rulers of the earth served the twice-born like merchants."

sanskrit: na sā śrīr devarājasya yamasya varuṇasya vā guhyakādhipater vāpi yā śrī rājan yudhiṣṭhire
english: "That prosperity is not found in the king of the gods, nor in Yama, nor in Varuṇa, nor even in the lord of the Guhyakas — that prosperity which, O king, is in Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍuputrasya śriyaṃ paramikām aham śāntiṃ na parigacchāmi dahyamānena cetasā
english: "Having seen that supreme prosperity of the son of Pāṇḍu, I find no peace, my heart burning."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca yām etām uttamāṃ lakṣmīṃ dṛṣṭavān asi pāṇḍave tasyāḥ prāptāv upāyaṃ me śṛṇu satyaparākrama
english: Śakuni said: "This supreme fortune you have seen in the Pāṇḍava — hear from me the means to win it, O you of true valor."

sanskrit: aham akṣeṣv abhijñātaḥ pṛthivyām api bhārata hṛdayajñaḥ paṇajñaś ca viśeṣajñaś ca devane
english: "I am expert in dice, O Bharata — even famed across the earth — knowing the hearts of players, knowing the stakes, knowing the distinctions in gambling."

sanskrit: dyūtapriyaś ca kaunteyo na ca jānāti devitum āhūtaś caiṣyati vyaktaṃ dīvyāvety āhvayasva tam
english: "The son of Kuntī loves dice yet does not know how to play. When summoned, he will clearly come. Invite him, saying: let us play."
